segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Welcome to Psalm Nights. [pause 15]

Lie back. Let the pillow take your head. Let your breathing find its own pace. [pause 15]

Tonight's psalm is one of the shortest in the Bible. Psalm 131. Only three verses. It is a psalm for people who think too much at night. [pause 15]

We will read it slowly, and then again. [pause 17]

verses.text: A Song of degrees of David. LORD, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.
Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.
Let Israel hope in the LORD from henceforth and for ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
The psalmist says he does not busy himself with great matters, with things too high for him. [pause 22]

Some things are too big to figure out tonight. The psalm gives you permission to put them down. You do not have to understand everything before you can rest. [pause 25]

Then comes the picture of a weaned child. Not a baby crying to be fed, but a little one who is full and content, leaning against her mother. Quiet. Calm. Just there. [pause 25]

That is the picture of a soul at rest in God. Not because every question is answered. Because you are held. [pause 27]

Two companion passages now. [pause 21]

verses.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.
To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David. Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.
Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Come unto me, all who are weary and heavy laden. Jesus said it to tired people. He did not ask them to be less tired first. [pause 23]

In returning and rest, Isaiah says. In quietness and confidence, strength. Quiet is not weakness. It can be strength. [pause 25]

And two more from the Psalms. My soul waits in silence for God. And, return to your rest, O my soul. You can say that to yourself tonight. Return to your rest. [pause 27]

Here is Psalm 131 again. Three verses. Let them be slow. [pause 29]

verses.text: A Song of degrees of David. LORD, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.
Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.
Let Israel hope in the LORD from henceforth and for ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
We will stop here. [pause 8]

Let the room be dark and still around you. Let the pillow be cool. [pause 10]

You have read his words tonight. You can stop thinking about them now and simply rest in them. [pause 12]

Every part of you that is tired, let it be tired. You do not have to be strong right now. [pause 15]

He is awake, so you can sleep. [pause 15]

Let the last words you heard tonight be the ones that stay. Let the rest drift away. [pause 20]

It is all right to stop now. [pause 20]

Rest well. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Every psalm and companion is stored KJV pasted by code; reflections paraphrase in short echoes (no 8+ word typed scripture) and stay with each psalm's own point (shepherd, evening rest, keeping, shelter, stillness, quiet soul, being known, waiting, a shield in flight, light and waiting). No promise of sleep or protection: Psalm 91 says plainly it does not promise nothing hard will happen; Proverbs 3:24 framed as 'not a promise for every night'. God never quoted in first person outside scripture. Headings (Ps 3, Absalom) used only as the text's own titles.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a tired woman at 11 PM can follow; no filler, no church jargon unexplained; hospital and grief named gently; shared rests vary their wording so the close is not the same sentence every night; pacing tuned only by silence (pauses) to 13.5-13.7 min voiced at the measured 117 wpm.
